name: Emperor Hsüan-tsung
bio: Emperor Hsüan-tsung (AD 685–761), known as Ming Huang, reigned from 713 to 755.
The poems here are Witter Bynner’s versions, from the texts of Kiang Kang-hu, in The Jade Mountain (1929).

poems.title: I Pass through the Lu Dukedom with a Sigh and a Sacrifice for Confucius
poems.author: Emperor Hsüan-tsung
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
O Master, how did the world repay
Your life of long solicitude? —
The Lords of Tsou have misprized your land,
And your home has been used as the palace of Lu... .
You foretold that when phœnixes vanished, your fortunes too would end,
You knew that the captured unicorn would be a sign of the close of your teaching... .
Can this sacrifice I watch, here between two temple-pillars,
Be the selfsame omen of death you dreamed of long ago?

poems.title: 幸蜀回至劍門 (Xing shu hui zhi jian men)
poems.author: Emperor Hsüan-tsung
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
劍閣橫雲峻，鑾輿出狩回。
翠屏千仞合，丹嶂五丁開。
灌木縈旗轉，仙雲拂馬來。
乘時方在德，嗟爾勒銘才。

poems.title: 經鄒魯祭孔子而嘆之 (Jing zou lu ji kong zi er tan zhi)
poems.author: Emperor Hsüan-tsung
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
夫子何爲者，棲棲一代中。
地猶鄹氏邑，宅即魯王宮。
嘆鳳嗟身否，傷麟怨道窮。
今看兩楹奠，當與夢時同。
